record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.context_brief: zero-dimensional CDH spaces with non-CDH squares
record.original_question: Is there, in ZFC, a zero-dimensional countable dense homogeneous space X whose square X^2 is not countable dense homogeneous?

evidence.quote: Problem 14 (Medini [58]). Is there (in ZFC) a zero-dimensional CDH space X such that X2 is not CDH?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological space $X$ is said to be countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if for every pair of countable dense subsets $D, E \subseteq X$ there exists a homeomorphism $h : X \to X$ with $h(D) = E$. A space is zero-dimensional if it has a base consisting of clopen sets.

Does there exist, provably in ZFC (i.e., without additional set-theoretic assumptions beyond the standard Zermelo–Fraenkel axioms with choice), a zero-dimensional CDH space $X$ such that the product $X \times X$ is not countable dense homogeneous?
artifact.status_search_result: A 2024 preprint constructs in ZFC a zero-dimensional metrizable CDH space $X$ whose square $X^2$ is not CDH, explicitly stating that the construction works in ZFC (improving on an earlier MA(σ-centered) construction by Medini). Thus the problem appears to have been answered affirmatively. Additional set-theoretic hypotheses are only needed to make the example co-analytic.

status_evidence.title: Zero-dimensional metrizable CDH space X such that X^2 is not CDH
status_evidence.snippet: our construction works in ZFC and uses more elementary tools
status_evidence.claim: A ZFC construction of a zero-dimensional metrizable CDH space whose square is not CDH is presented.

status_evidence.title: Zero-dimensional metrizable CDH space X such that X2 is not CDH (ResearchGate)
status_evidence.snippet: A metrizable zero-dimensional CDH space X such that X^2 has exactly c countable dense subsets is constructed, answering a question of Medini.
status_evidence.claim: The construction answers Medini's question about a CDH space with non-CDH square.
